name: Crown Wire & Cable Co Inc
old_description: By using this website, you agree to our use of cookies. We use cookies to provide you with a great experience and to help our website run effectively.
about:
Crown Wire & Cable Co. Inc. was founded in 1986 in Millville, New Jersey, located in the Millville Airport complex about 30 miles south of Philadelphia. The company began as a supplier to the oil, gas, and water industries and has grown into one of the largest stocking distributors of steel wire rope and submersible pump cable in the United States.

The company stocks a broad range of products including submersible pump cable in multiple constructions (flat jacketed, neoprene, PVC twisted, flat parallel, round double jacketed), steel wire rope in various configurations (6x7 sand line, 6x21 drilling line, 19x7 rotation resistant, 6x36 winch cable, 6x25 casing/tubing line, 6x19 rotary drill line), galvanized and Type 304 stainless steel aircraft cable, and manila rope. It also sources related electrical products such as URD, SER, overhead, triplex, quadraplex, and irrigation cables on request. Crown Wire ships nationwide and serves international markets in Central America, South America, and the Caribbean.

Primary customers operate in the oil and gas, water well, and electrical utility sectors. The company’s technical staff assists with product selection for applications ranging from submersible pump installations to drilling and winching operations. Crown Wire emphasizes 24/7 availability, with dedicated personnel reachable around the clock to handle inquiries and track shipments.

Crown Wire’s stated mission is to build long-term relationships through enhanced service, clear shipping communications, and superior products. The founders aimed to provide a pleasant, polite experience regardless of order size, a principle that continues to guide the company’s customer‑service approach.

name: Crystal Farms Dairy Co.
old_description: From potluck-perfect apps to easy-peasy weekday dinners, and everything in between.
about:
Crystal Farms Dairy Co. is headquartered in Edina, Minnesota. The company's roots trace to the 1920s when Nathan Friedell founded Nathan's Produce Company, and to the 1930s when Julius Rosenberg started an egg business after immigrating from Russia. The two operations merged in the 1970s, creating the Crystal Farms brand that sells cheese and other dairy products today.

The company produces a wide range of dairy items including shredded, block, sliced, and snack cheeses, ricotta, specialty cheeses, cream cheese, butter, English muffins, and bagels. Crystal Farms states that it sources its dairy from the Midwest and emphasizes a quality process that runs from ingredient selection through finished‑product inspection.

Crystal Farms primarily serves consumer retail and foodservice channels. The brand also engages with community partners: it supports the national FFA organization and its Minnesota, Wisconsin, and Iowa chapters; donates products quarterly to the Ronald McDonald House; and supplies nearly all cheese and butter for All Square, a Minneapolis non‑profit grilled‑cheese shop that employs formerly incarcerated individuals.

The company says its Midwestern dairy heritage and a culture of commitment — from high‑quality ingredients to careful final inspection — are what set it apart, allowing customers to "cheese like a Midwesterner."

name: Curbside Apparel
old_description: Curbside Apparel is a full-service screen printing shop on a mission to provide dignified employment and job skills training to people transitioning out of homelessness.
about:
Curbside Apparel operates in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma, as an employment program of the Homeless Alliance, a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization. The social enterprise was established to provide dignified employment and job skills training to individuals transitioning out of homelessness, though a specific founding year is not publicly disclosed. The program is structured around a paid screen printing certification that equips participants with marketable skills.

The shop functions as a full-service screen printing facility, producing custom shirts, hoodies, tote bags, and posters. It offers in-house graphic design and fulfillment services, handling orders ranging from 20 posters up to 20,000 shirts. Production details such as facility size and headcount are not published.

Customers include local businesses, schools, faith-based organizations, sports teams, restaurants, and retail stores seeking branded apparel and promotional items. Each order supports the program's participants through paid work and ongoing training, with revenue also funding broader services like housing assistance and case management.

The company's stated purpose is to turn purchases into tools for social change, directly funding job opportunities, income, and supportive services for people experiencing homelessness in Oklahoma City. By integrating commercial production with a supportive employment model, Curbside Apparel aims to demonstrate how everyday procurement decisions can create measurable community impact.

name: Current Electronics
old_description: Current Electronics provides custom product design, electronics
about:
Current Electronics, Inc. operates from Kansas City, Missouri, with all production kept in the United States. The company provides custom product design, electronics engineering, and manufacturing services focused on durability and performance.

The shop specializes in low- to medium-volume and prototype printed circuit board assembly, backed by automated assembly equipment capable of fine-pitch BGA placement. It offers both full and partial turn-key production, handling everything from design consultation and parts procurement to final product assembly, visual inspection, and optional operational testing. Engineering services span concept development, project management, and design-build execution through to finished goods.

Customers come primarily from the automotive sector, where the firm handles ESD and EMI hardening, as well as from IoT and connected-device programs such as Cat M1 cellular integration, GPS tracking, Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, and touch-sensor controls. Recent projects also include accelerometer-based motion sensing and iOS applications with HomeKit certification.

The business was built around the need for rapid, precise realization of electronic designs, emphasizing thorough attention at every step to ensure the job is done right the first time.

Custom Craft Inc operates from West Warwick, Rhode Island, where it has produced outdoor cushions and related products for nearly three decades. The business began with a focus on high‑quality, fashionable cushions designed to withstand the elements.

The firm manufactures outdoor cushions, pads, umbrellas, canopies, and pillows using durable all‑weather fabrics and modern techniques. It offers custom‑crafting variations on standard styles and specializes in sizing for non‑standard items. No facility size, headcount, or annual volume figures are provided.

Custom Craft serves outdoor furniture manufacturers, retailers, and specialty patio stores throughout the northeastern United States. Its products are used as replacements for wicker, teak, wrought iron, aluminum, and rattan furniture. Specific customers mentioned include Bryant Industries and WHS Industries.

The company emphasizes personal service, flexibility, and expedited turnaround as key differentiators, along with a focus on selection, quality, and price. Its family‑owned structure allows direct attention to each order.

name: Custom Food Equipment
old_description: Let CFE survey your existing setup to see if maybe its time to make your line more efficient. Saving you lots of Ca$h.
about:
Custom Food Equipment (CFE) operates from Orange, California, where a team of professionals designs and builds commercial stainless steel refrigerated food equipment. The company focuses on open-top speed-line units for food service operations.

CFE’s product line includes pan chillers, drawer replacement modules, pizza stations, hot food warming equipment, equipment stands, and prep tables. All units are fabricated from heavy-gauge 304 stainless steel with all-welded construction and feature a proprietary chilled pressure chamber (CPC) system that the company says provides 30 percent more heat-transfer material for consistent temperature control. Additional features include vapor control, CFC-free insulation, and customized utility connections.

The equipment is sold to commercial kitchens, restaurants, and food preparation lines that require reliable cold-holding and hot-holding solutions. CFE also offers site surveys to evaluate existing lines for efficiency improvements.

The company emphasizes energy-saving design and patent-pending CPC technology as its core differentiators, aiming to deliver precise, dependable cooling performance while reducing operating costs.

name: Custom Furniture & Design LLC
old_description: Built with skill, care, and decades of experience; custom furniture and cabinetry designed to last for generations.
about:
Custom Furniture & Design LLC has operated from Bantam, Connecticut since its founding in 1989. The company was established as a woodworking shop serving the surrounding region and has remained in the same location for over three decades.

The shop produces custom cabinetry, bespoke furniture, and architectural millwork for residential projects. Using traditional joinery and hand-selected premium hardwoods, the team fabricates kitchen systems, bathroom vanities, built-in storage, dining tables, sideboards, bedroom suites, library shelving, coffered ceilings, wainscoting, and custom entryways. All work moves from raw lumber through finishing and installation in-house, with no outsourced fabrication.

Clients include homeowners, interior designers, architects, and builders across Litchfield County, Fairfield County, and Lower Westchester. The company collaborates on projects ranging from whole-kitchen suites to individual furniture pieces, working from client drawings or developing details jointly.

The firm emphasizes single-source accountability: design, build, and installation are handled by the same crew, ensuring that each piece fits the specific architecture of the home rather than adapting catalog dimensions. This approach was built on the premise that cabinetry should be made for the space, not pulled from a standard line.
